title: Yet venials with mortals in the damned draw everlasting penalty (Thomas)
source_text: XIX. Porro quamvis communis Scholae Romanae doctrina sit peccatum veniale natura sua mortem aeternam non mereri, docet illa nihilominus peccatum veniale aeterna poena puniri, in iis qui cum peccato mortali ex hac vita decedunt, & inferis adjudicantur. Idque post Thomam Aquinatem, qui asserit peccato veniali deberi poenam aeternam, si cum peccato mortali inveniatur in aliquo damnato, quia in inferno nulla potest esse remissio. In 1.2. quaest. 87. art. 5. in 3. arg.
pass_a_gloss: Further, although the common doctrine of the Roman School is that venial sin by its own nature does not merit eternal death, it teaches nonetheless that venial sin is punished with eternal penalty in those who depart this life with mortal sin and are adjudged to hell. And that after Thomas Aquinas, who asserts that eternal punishment is due to venial sin if it is found with mortal sin in someone damned, because in hell there can be no remission. In 1a2ae, question 87, article 5, on the third argument.
pass_b_english: Even while denying venial sin merits hell of itself, the School teaches it is punished eternally in those who die in mortal sin.
Thomas: with mortal sin in the damned, venial draws endless penalty because hell has no remission.
